collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VII: KNOWLEDGE, CONSENT AND SHARED WORK (LCG-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume III concepts (201-300): weather readers and navigators, seed keepers and terrace builders, permission and consent, who leads and who is heard, homes built by many hands, songs for the uncelebrated, and a village writing its own story.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Children challenge the old rule that they may not swim in the lagoon at dusk: explain the rule, or rethink it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) and the other children want to know why they are not allowed to swim in the lagoon at dusk. Nobody can remember. (friend) says it is the rule, and rules are rules. (subject) says that is not a reason. What should (friend) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) asks the elders. It turns out the rule began when sharks came into the lagoon at dusk, long ago, before the reef shifted. They have not come for thirty years. The rule is changed. (subject) is the first in the water.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) says the rule stays, reason or not. The children are cross. Then one evening they see a long grey shadow in the lagoon at dusk, and nobody argues about the rule again.
